prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Offshore wind O&M; scope to Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere); excludes public grid, non-farm port ops. Wildmere: boundary/dispatch/status; Export Limit Advisory when capability<target; applies accepted ceiling, records time. Turbine Controller (Glassfin): validated commands within protections, blocks conflicts, safe mode on auxiliary loss; Pitch Deviation Notice. Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor feed Turbine Sensor Bus. Offshore Substation (Morrowick): Main Transformer, export cable, Export Cable Monitor, station service transformers, Fire Detection Panel; Transformer Tap Snapshot→Shore Control Room; mode Substation Degraded. Substation Operator: approved switching, clearances, escalates alarms, notifies Grid Dispatcher. Emergency Generator (Foxglove): auto-start on auxiliary loss, no unapproved paralleling, sheds loads; Start Test Trace. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale): time-stamped/operating data→Shore Control Room (Amber Quay); Session Revocation Receipt→Cybersecurity Gateway. Shore Control Room: dispatch target/ramp, keeps last validated limit on grid comms loss; monitors turbine status, records survey restrictions. Grid Dispatcher: targets; priority safety>protection>export. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard): Position Quality Flag. Mode Grid Constraint. Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown): Squall Window Bulletin, Deferred Task Rationale (used by Field Supervisor for postponed cyber work); proposes survey dates. Duty Planner: mobilization (CTV/Daughter Craft/SOV/Helideck), confirms inspection priority, Transfer Manifest Addendum→Vessel Master. CTV: Harness Audit Card. Weather Analyst: Wave Burst Record. Weather Service, Metocean Buoy: forecasts/measurements. Port Agent: Berth Slot Confirmation. Redoubt (permit control) blocks release. Vessel Master: headcount reconciliation, Crew Count Correction. Personnel Tracking Console; North/South Access Scanner; accountability at transfer/disembark. Field Supervisor: confirms party, cyber items in briefing, escalates→Marine Coordinator. Cybersecurity Gateway monitors traffic; Cybersecurity Analyst: alerts, Firmware Hash Attestation, preserves evidence. Incident lead classifies/assigns reports; containment isolates only affected service safely; recovery after containment confirmed; SCADA Engineer validates restoration; actions logged time/location/role/disposition. Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur): Leading Edge Tile Image (linked turbine/blade/date/angle/conditions) in approved operating state; Blade Specialist classifies;

Document units:
S450: Close-access work is planned only after the responsible team verifies turbine isolation, rotor restraint, access arrangements, and rescue provisions.
S451: The HSE Officer reviews the work method, exposure controls, and emergency arrangements before personnel approach the rotor.
S452: The Blade Specialist examines the affected surface using suitable lighting, measurement tools, and nondestructive inspection methods.
S453: Defect records describe location, dimensions, orientation, suspected cause, confidence, and any change from earlier observations.
S454: Cracks, erosion, coating loss, lightning damage, bond-line indications, and drainage concerns are assessed against approved engineering criteria.
S455: The Blade Specialist distinguishes cosmetic damage from conditions that could affect structural integrity or safe turbine operation.
S456: When evidence is incomplete, the inspection record identifies the uncertainty and specifies additional measurements or imagery needed.
S457: The Field Supervisor confirms that close-access findings are documented before personnel leave the work area.
S458: The Maintenance Planning Engine uses the assessed severity, defect growth rate, weather exposure, and production impact to support repair prioritization.
S459: The Duty Planner assigns a target repair window and coordinates required personnel, equipment, and vessel capacity.
S460: The Storekeeper checks repair materials and tooling against the approved repair method before mobilization.
S461: The Service Operations Vessel prepares the Recovery Basket Load Sheet for the planned work activity.
S462: Repair plans identify surface preparation, material application, cure requirements, inspection hold points, and acceptance criteria.
S463: After repair, the Blade Specialist records the completed work and verifies that the repaired area meets the applicable acceptance criteria.
S464: The Duty Planner updates the maintenance record and schedules follow-up inspection when residual uncertainty or defect history warrants it.
S465: Port and berth coordination aligns vessel access with the readiness of offshore work, people, equipment, and permits.
S466: The Marine Coordinator maintains a rolling view of berth occupancy, planned arrivals, departure estimates, and vessel service requirements.
S467: Berth capacity is assessed against usable quay length, water depth, access routes, lifting arrangements, and local safety clearances.
S468: The port schedule includes time for arrival checks, passenger movements, cargo handling, refueling, and routine vessel servicing.
S469: The Duty Planner compares task readiness with the expected departure window before committing crews and equipment to a marine campaign.
S470: The Maintenance Planning Engine supports this review by presenting task duration, resource demand, and dependency status.
